problem: During active assistant playback, cancellation and reentry may preserve later user input while losing the semantically critical beginning of an overlapping user interruption. This is inbound interruption-onset conservation, distinct from the already-routed outbound heard-prefix/playout-grounding invariant.

external_falsifier_source.title: Overcoming State Inertia in Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models via Activation Steering
external_falsifier_source.source_scope: External primary research only; its model-specific mechanism and reported numbers are not F2 evidence. The reusable item is the Zero-Buffer failure shape: immediate interruption comprehension can lose initial input during speaking-to-listening transition.

smallest_candidate_discriminator.fixture_shape: Deterministic overlapping-turn sequence with active assistant output and a user interruption whose first lexical/semantic unit changes the intended meaning (negation, correction, stop or contrast). Bind exact input segment/packet identities across the interruption boundary.
must_observe: presence of the first semantic/lexical unit after admission
no duplicate durable memory/effect commit from the cancelled generation
smallest_candidate_discriminator.acceptance: PASS only if the admitted interruption onset is conserved through cancellation/reentry and no stale/duplicate durable authority is exercised. Fail closed on ambiguous segment identity or unbound timing.
smallest_candidate_discriminator.escalation: Repository discriminator first. Target/audio runtime only if repository mapping shows a real uncovered boundary and a current owner-authorized execution surface exists.
